decisions.decision: Use a data version repository to reproduce historical forecasts
decisions.context: Forecasts must be reproducible for any past week, so each run needs a recoverable data version. The design space offers repository-based versioning, code-repository versioning, or no data versioning (d:11).
decisions.rationale: A dedicated data version repository best supports retrieving the data used for a given historical forecast. The checked design point had no warnings, though it was unattested in this source-free design space.
consequences: Record the data version with each forecast run.
Maintain storage and retention for historical data versions.

decisions.decision: Use scheduled batch processing and training for weekly forecasts
decisions.context: The system produces weekly store and product forecasts, making a scheduled batch workflow a direct fit. The design space distinguishes batch from stream processing and batch from incremental learning (d:15, d:19).

alternatives.label: Batch-based learning
cons: Model updates await next training run

decisions.rationale: Weekly forecasts do not require real-time processing in the brief, so scheduled batches keep the workflow aligned with the delivery cadence. Choose batch-based learning as well for repeatable retraining; these are separate design dimensions (d:15, d:19).
consequences: Run forecast generation on a weekly schedule.
Reruns need the original data and model inputs.

decisions.decision: Serve forecasts as scheduled batch outputs
decisions.context: The required output is a weekly forecast per store and product; the brief specifies no real-time prediction interface. The design space includes scheduled batch serving and precomputed forecast delivery (d:5).
decisions.rationale: Scheduled batch serving directly represents processing forecasts on schedule and writing them to storage. It fits weekly outputs and allows the system to retain forecast results for prior weeks.
consequences: Define storage and lookup conventions for consumers.

decisions.decision: Use CI/CD to test and release model components
decisions.context: A three-person team owns the pipeline, and new model ideas should reach production quickly without breaking the weekly run. The design space covers CI/CD automation and what it builds and deploys (d:8, d:25).

alternatives.label: Build, test, and deploy models to be served and other system components

decisions.rationale: CI/CD supports frequent, repeatable releases for a small team; configure it to build and test served models and related components (d:25, v:25.1). Testing trained model quality is also a relevant pipeline test (d:26, v:26.9). The selected combination was checked with no warnings, but the design point is unattested.
consequences: Keep release configuration and pipeline definitions maintained.

decisions.decision: Keep rollback available and track deployed models
decisions.context: New model ideas must reach production without disrupting the weekly run, so releases need a recovery path and production tracking. The design space includes rollback and tracking choices (d:10, d:22).

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
pros: Limits impact of a poor release

decisions.rationale: Rollback gives the team a direct response when a new model threatens the weekly run. Pair it with model in-production tracking (d:22, v:22.4) to record usage, inputs, and outputs; these are separate dimensions in the checked point.
consequences: Retain the previous deployable model version.
Record model identity and run inputs alongside forecasts.
